leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight round-1 configurations name B010 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock). They share the same two laureates, the view that independent reproduction across JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and NPL settles maturity, and a citation centred on the magic-wavelength lattice and clocks near 1e-18. They differ in emphasis: some stress metrology and tests of fundamental physics, Lindroth stresses the atomic-structure theory behind the systematics, and Eriksson, Lindroth and Pearce each concede in their own files that this is a measurement capability more than a discovery of a new phenomenon. Eriksson (from B051), Johansson (from B041) and Pearce (from B061) moved to B010 after the opening ballots, so this support is not independent of the discussion. Shared reservations: distinctness from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, the pending SI redefinition, and uncredited contributors (Lemonde, Takamoto, Hollberg, ion-clock groups). The exact citation wording is not settled.

One configuration names B061 (Halzen, Karle, Spiering, IceCube). The case is a discovery made in nature: a diffuse TeV-PeV flux seen in 2013, since confirmed in several channels, with partial source identification (TXS 0506+056, Galactic plane). The supporter himself names attribution within a large collaboration and the unidentified origin of most of the flux as the main weaknesses. Pearce ranked it first at opening and now lists it only as an alternative; no other member's preferred configuration includes it.

One configuration names B047 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (omitting Hasan), cited for the quantum spin Hall prediction, the Z2 classification and the HgTe realisation. The case is a clean, well-understood mechanism with a complete theory-to-experiment chain. Mehlig concedes that the allocation leaves out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and Hasan, and that the 2016 topological-phases prize may make it look redundant; he lists B010 as a genuine alternative.

One configuration names B039 (Rose, Urban, Haider, aberration-corrected TEM). The case is that it broke the Scherzer limit, is mature and has a compact attribution. Olsson discloses field proximity, says she would not insist if a fair prize cannot be built from these three names, and the omitted STEM-corrector line (Krivanek, Dellby) and the instrument-versus-discovery question remain open.

areas_of_agreement: Five of eight members explicitly prefer B010 as their configuration with the identical two laureates, Katori and Ye, and no member disputes the reproducibility of the roughly 1e-18 lattice-clock results.

Every proposer of B010 describes its attribution as the cleanest on the shortlist, with Katori credited for the magic-wavelength proposal and first demonstrations and Ye for record accuracy and the many-body regime.

Members who address IceCube accept that the diffuse flux is a secure detection; the disagreement is about attribution among Halzen, Karle and Spiering and about source identification, not about whether the flux is real.
Members who discuss B051 agree it has opened a field but that the superconducting pairing mechanism is unresolved and that Cao and others sit outside the credited names.
Members repeatedly ask that the expert reports settle priority and decisive contribution before the final ballot.
scientific_disputes: Whether a measurement capability such as the lattice clock counts as the kind of discovery the committee should reward, compared with a new phenomenon in nature (B061, B047, B051); Eriksson, Lindroth and Pearce raise this against their own preference.

Whether the TXS 0506+056 and Galactic-plane results show that the cosmic-ray origin question is being answered or only that a flux exists, and whether independent telescopes (ANTARES, Baikal, KM3NeT) confirm the diffuse flux strongly enough.

Whether the 1e-18 claims for strontium lattice clocks are independent of blackbody-shift and lattice-light-shift systematics (asked by Eriksson), and what the lattice clock has revealed that earlier clocks could not (asked by Danielsson).
Whether the pairing mechanism and the role of strain and disorder in magic-angle graphene must be understood before B051 is considered ready.
Whether aberration-corrected TEM carries enough physics content, and whether the TEM corrector (Rose, Haider, Urban) and STEM corrector (Krivanek, Dellby) lines can be separated cleanly.
attribution_disputes: B010: all proposers agree on Katori and Ye, but Lemonde, Takamoto, Hollberg, the Kimble-era magic-wavelength discussion and the Al+/Yb+ ion-clock groups lie outside them; Olsson asks how Katori's original proposal should be weighed against Ye's record accuracy, and several members want the citation worded around the lattice scheme so it stays accurate.

B061: Halzen, Karle and Spiering come from a collaboration of hundreds with AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND precursors; Danielsson, Olsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce all say three names are hard to defend, and several want the expert reports to say who was decisive for the 2013 observation rather than for construction.

B047: Mehlig and Olsson differ on the third name, Molenkamp versus Hasan; Mehlig would resist dropping Mele, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) are outside the credited names in either case.
B051: the lead experimental authors Cao and Fatemi and earlier twist theory are outside the credited names (noted by Eriksson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce).
B019: Kroll asks whether the five-name Hubbard-simulation credit can be cut to three without excluding Zoller and Cirac.
maturity_disputes: B010: the SI second has not been redefined. Kroll cites its preparation as evidence of impact but lists it as an uncertainty, while Eriksson, Johansson and Pearce say the science does not depend on it and Lindroth asks that it be kept separate; Johansson notes the cleanest narrative moment may lie a few years ahead.
B061: source identification is still thin, so Olsson regards recognition as arguably early, while Danielsson regards the diffuse flux observed more than a decade ago as the discovery itself.

B051: the pairing mechanism and the role of strain and disorder are still disputed (Mehlig, Lindroth, Johansson, Eriksson, Pearce); several treat this as a maturity concern rather than a question of importance.
B047 and B041: timing is questioned relative to the 2016 topological-phases prize (Danielsson, Mehlig) and the 2025 circuit prize (Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, close to the superconducting-circuit community) says he should be recused or discount his view on B041; he lists it only as an alternative. Kroll notes his own WACQT leadership overlaps institutionally with Chalmers on B041, which bears on his alternative rather than his preference.
Olsson (head of a Chalmers electron-microscopy group) flags field proximity to B039, is the only member to prefer it, and defers to the chair on whether recusal is warranted.

Danielsson reports no apparent conflict on B061 but cannot verify from his profile whether Uppsala has institutional involvement in neutrino astronomy, and says he would recuse from B061 if the committee found one.

Pearce (the chair, writing this summary) works in astroparticle physics at KTH and belongs to the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations; he is not an IceCube member as far as his profile shows, and flags B061 as close to his field and B012 and B057 only as shared detector expertise.
Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory during his PhD, in the same JILA environment as Ye, with no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye, and reports no decisive conflict on B010.

Eriksson notes a shared electronic-structure theory community with MacDonald (B051) but no direct link; Lindroth reports no tie to any shortlisted candidate (her collaboration with L'Huillier concerns B054, which is not on this shortlist); Mehlig notes Chalmers colleagues but no tie to any credited candidate.
questions_for_round2: For B010, should the citation name the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and the 1e-18 regime explicitly, and does that wording make it distinct enough from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes?
For B010, what do the expert reports say about priority among Katori, Ye, Takamoto, Lemonde and the SYRTE group, and is the Katori and Ye pair defensible against the uncredited contributors?
For B061, who among Halzen, Karle and Spiering was decisive for the 2013 diffuse-flux observation, and have independent neutrino telescopes confirmed it strongly enough to settle maturity?

For B047, must the committee choose between Molenkamp and Hasan as third laureate, or is Kane, Mele and Molenkamp acceptable without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and Hasan, and does the 2016 prize make a second topological prize redundant?
Should the pending SI redefinition of the second influence the timing of B010, or be kept separate from the scientific case?
Should a measurement capability (B010, B039) be weighed against a discovery in nature (B061, B047, B051), and how should that be balanced against the clean attribution of B010?
Do members who prefer B061, B047 or B039 wish to move, and if not, what specific evidence or citation wording would change their preference?
Do the flagged proximities (Johansson on B041, Olsson on B039, Danielsson's Uppsala check on B061, and the chair on B061) require any recusal or discounting before the final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: The explicit round-1 preferences are B010 (five members), and B061, B047 and B039 (one member each). The B010 block includes members who moved after the opening ballots, and each of them states reservations about discovery content, overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and uncredited contributors. The minority configurations rest on a discovery in nature (B061, B047) or an instrument limit overcome (B039), and each minority proponent names attribution as the weakest point. Round 2 should test these reservations and the competing attribution questions against the expert reports rather than count positions.
